why: Count triplets by fixing the middle: (earlier values greater) x (later values smaller). Both counts are prefix counts over compressed value ranks, done with two Fenwick passes.
hints: Fix j as the middle element. How many choices for i and for k does it have?
left[j] = earlier values > nums[j], right[j] = later values < nums[j]; the answer is sum left[j] * right[j].
Compress values to ranks; one Fenwick pass left to right (seen - count of ranks <= r) and one right to left (count of ranks < r). O(n log n).
pitfalls: Strict inequalities: equal values count on neither side.
